summary:
The FDA's class-wide label change on 9 November is the biggest search wave of the week. It adds NAION, a rare optic-nerve condition, to Warnings and Precautions for every GLP-1 medicine, tirzepatide included. In the FDA's meta-analysis of 126 trials, NAION occurred at 6.4 cases per 100,000 person-years on GLP-1 medicines vs 3.8 on placebo or other diabetes drugs. Every major outlet has covered it: AP, Reuters, BBC, WSJ, CNN and the Washington Post. Creator coverage on YouTube is still mostly reactive and alarming, so a calm long-form built from the label ("Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Eye Warning: What Changed") fits our label-change search format and should be made first. A symptom Short should go with it.

Second: Foundayo (orforglipron) Phase 3 sleep-apnea data were presented at AHA on 9 November and published in JAMA. The apnea-hypopnea index fell by an average of 43.8% without PAP and 27.5% with PAP, and Lilly plans to file with the FDA by year-end. That refreshes 'foundayo', our best search term after EloraTZP. Single-trial deep dives are banned in long-form, so use it in a Short and as a hook for the label-only Foundayo what-to-expect long-form.

Third: ObesityWeek (14–17 November) may bring the full REDEFINE 4 results (CagriSema vs tirzepatide). This is the only clear EloraTZP-model opportunity coming up, so prepare a packaging template now and publish within 48 h of the presentation.

Thanksgiving on tirzepatide peaks from 18 to 27 November, so funnel Shorts should start now. Lane A evergreens hold steady and stay in playbook order:
- injection site
- pen how-to from the Instructions for Use
- alcohol
- burping and heartburn
- keeping results after stopping

The resistance-training RCT published in Nature Medicine on 9 November (UWA's T-REX trial: ages 50–70, no type 2 diabetes) is a fresh randomized hook. Use it in a Short that points to the Strength and Bones videos.

What I couldn't verify:
- I couldn't open the T-REX PubMed abstract, so its results are unchecked.
- I couldn't find any 2026 'double risk' study behind the Euronews headline on stopping. The supporting evidence is the March 2026 BMJ Medicine study in veterans with type 2 diabetes: an observational study that reports up to a 22% higher risk, not double. So frame stopping as a habits topic.

Rejected: compounded tirzepatide price reports, gray-market retatrutide, GLP-1 microdosing, and 'research-use' tirzepatide vial stories.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) eye warning explained: FDA's class-wide NAION label change (Nov 9). NAION occurred at 6.4 vs 3.8 cases per 100,000 person-years in the FDA's 126-trial meta-analysis
candidates.angle: Label-change explainer that stays calm and specific: what NAION is, what the label now says, what 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 person-years means in plain numbers (rare, and a 'potential' risk), the one symptom the FDA says to report right away (sudden, painless vision loss or a missing part of vision in one eye), and why you shouldn't stop on your own. Talk to your prescriber, and see an eye doctor promptly if symptoms appear. Credit NANOS and the AAO by name if quoted. Title: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Eye Warning: What Changed'. Thumbnail: big eye object plus 'HOW RARE?'.
candidates.predicted_peak: now to 7 days (search demand stays high for 2–3 weeks as patients ask prescribers)
candidates.why_now: The FDA ordered the label change on Nov 9. AP, Reuters, BBC, WSJ, CNN, CBS, USA Today and the Washington Post covered it Nov 9–11, and local TV is still picking it up on Nov 11. It is exactly the 'label or safety-labelling change' format named in our search-demand research. Patients now search the brand names plus 'eye' or 'vision', and most existing YouTube coverage is alarmist or from law firms.

evidence.signal: FDA requires class-wide GLP-1 RA labeling changes for potential NAION risk (Nov 9, 2026)
NAION added to Warnings and Precautions across the class, tirzepatide included; meta-analysis of 126 trials, 6.4 vs 3.8 per 100,000 person-years
Prescribers should tell patients to report sudden, painless vision loss right away and refer to an ophthalmologist
Mainstream and trade pickup
New review of ocular safety of GLP-1 RAs

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and vision: which eye symptoms mean call now (the new NAION label language)
candidates.angle: 08:00 body-worry Short: 'Blurry vision on tirzepatide: is this normal?' Separate the common, usually temporary blurry vision linked to blood-sugar changes (diabetes labels mention diabetic retinopathy complications in people with type 2 diabetes) from the new label's red flag: sudden, painless vision loss or a missing part of vision in one eye, which needs care right away. One new fact: the rate is about 6 in 100,000 person-years. Use your local urgent care or emergency number. Don't stop on your own; talk to your prescriber.
keywords: is blurry vision normal on mounjaro
candidates.why_now: The label change is driving felt-symptom searches. People who notice any eye change now google it. Our proven Short format (calm 'Is this normal?' with tirzepatide in the title) fits exactly.

evidence.signal: Class-wide NAION warning, Nov 9
'What GLP-1 users should know' consumer framing, with symptoms: sudden vision loss in one eye, blurred vision, blind spots

candidates.topic: ObesityWeek 2026 (Nov 14–17): did CagriSema beat tirzepatide? Full REDEFINE 4 (open-label, 84 weeks, adults with obesity)
candidates.angle: EloraTZP model: 'Did CagriSema Beat Tirzepatide?' long-form published within 48 h of the full presentation. Topline already public: 23.0% vs 25.5% if everyone stayed on treatment, and non-inferiority not met. Give both arms, open-label, the population, and side effects. CagriSema isn't approved; talk to your prescriber. Pre-build the packaging and beat list now and fill in the numbers on presentation day.
candidates.why_now: This is the only randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide on the near calendar. It has appeared in 6 of our snapshots. Our EloraTZP result shows that timing is what decides it: the evergreen CagriSema video got only 105 min.

evidence.signal: Seen 6 times across 3 topic variants, momentum 70–80

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) and sleep apnea: Phase 3 at AHA 2026 and in JAMA (Nov 9). AHI fell by an average of 43.8% without PAP and 27.5% with PAP at 52 weeks; FDA filing planned by year-end
candidates.angle: 13:00 lead Short: 'Can the Foundayo pill help sleep apnea?' Give what's confirmed: adults with obesity or overweight and moderate-to-severe OSA, compared with placebo, the average AHI drop in each arm, and that it isn't yet approved for sleep apnea. Point to the label-only 'Foundayo (orforglipron): what to expect' long-form (approved-drug search long), which gives one line to this result as a hook.
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–10 days; second spike at the FDA filing
candidates.why_now: Phase 3 was presented at AHA on Nov 9 and published in JAMA, with MedPage, Medscape (Nov 11), Time and Medical Xpress covering it. 'foundayo' is our top search term after EloraTZP. Few creators have covered the OSA data yet.

evidence.signal: Phase 3 met its primary endpoint; AHI −43.8% (no PAP), −27.5% (PAP); FDA submission by end of 2026
Oral GLP-1 reduces OSA severity and improves cardiometabolic risk factors
Up to a 44% average reduction in breathing interruptions

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: feeling full fast, protein first, smaller plates, eating slower, easing nausea at a big meal
candidates.angle: 20:00 funnel Shorts pointing to the existing Thanksgiving long-form. Each gives one fresh practical question: 'Why do I feel sick after a few bites on tirzepatide?', 'Leftovers on tirzepatide: what helps', 'What to say when family asks why you're not eating'. Never mention holiday dates in evergreen parts.
candidates.why_now: A seasonal spike is about to start. Seen in 11 snapshots with momentum rising to 93. The playbook asks for funnel Shorts 2 days ahead of the peak.

evidence.signal: 11 appearances, momentum 86→93

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide injection site reactions: what's normal (redness, itching, small lumps), label rates per dose, and when to call your prescriber
candidates.angle: Lane A long: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Injection Site Reactions: Normal?' Give label rates per dose (6% at 5 mg, 8% at 10 and 15 mg vs about 2% on placebo). Explain why rotating sites helps (per the IFU) and that serious allergic reactions are post-marketing reports with their own emergency instruction. Open with a 'you' scenario.
candidates.why_now: First in the playbook's Lane A order. Two Shorts are proven (237 views, and 119 by day 1–2). The long-form needs to be live before people start their pens over the holidays.

evidence.signal: Injection-site reaction rates by dose vs placebo

candidates.topic: How to use the tirzepatide pen: injection sites, rotation and common mistakes, per the Instructions for Use (Zepbound/Mounjaro single-dose pen and KwikPen)
candidates.angle: Device how-to search long, using the IFU only: where you can inject (belly, thigh, back of upper arm if someone else injects), rotating sites, letting it reach room temperature as the IFU states, holding until the second click, and what to do if you see a drop. No amounts, no dosing. Ask your pharmacist or prescriber to show you.
candidates.predicted_peak: steady; New Year starters spike in early January
candidates.why_now: Device how-tos are one of the formats that beat channel averages 10–195x in this niche. KwikPen rollout questions keep coming, and injection-site Shorts are proven for us.

evidence.signal: Official step-by-step pen instructions and injection sites

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and alcohol at holiday parties: what the label says, why a drink may hit differently, and the low-blood-sugar caveat for people on insulin or sulfonylureas
candidates.angle: Lane A long: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) and Alcohol: What to Know'. Cover what the label covers (dehydration and GI effects, low-blood-sugar risk with insulin or sulfonylureas), what research is exploring (incretins and alcohol use, which is early), and why there's no 'safe amount' we can give. Ask your prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Party season starts. Seen in 4 snapshot variants. A new systematic review on incretins for alcohol use disorder (Ther Adv Psychopharmacol) and a target trial emulation (Diabetes Obes Metab, Nov 3) refresh the hook.

evidence.signal: Systematic review: incretin therapies for alcohol use disorder

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide burping and heartburn: why slower gastric emptying causes sulfur burps and reflux after big meals, and what helps
candidates.angle: Lane A long: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Burping and Heartburn: What Helps'. Use label rates for eructation and GERD in both arms, and the mechanism (slower stomach emptying). Practical steps: smaller meals, stop eating when full, avoid lying down after eating. Name when to call (severe or won't go away, or severe stomach pain because of the pancreatitis caveat). Ties into Thanksgiving week.
candidates.why_now: In the playbook's Lane A order. Heavy holiday meals amplify the symptom searches.

evidence.signal: GI adverse reaction rates, including eructation and GERD, vs placebo

candidates.topic: Strength training on tirzepatide: new randomized trial in Nature Medicine (Nov 9) on resistance exercise and lean mass during tirzepatide treatment (UWA T-REX: men and postmenopausal women aged 50–70, no type 2 diabetes)
candidates.angle: 20:00 funnel Short pointing to Strength and Bones & Muscle: 'Does lifting weights on tirzepatide protect muscle?' Give the randomized result vs usual activity as averages, with the exact population. Verify the numbers from the full paper first; I couldn't fetch the abstract.
candidates.predicted_peak: 5–14 days as science press catches up
candidates.why_now: A fresh randomized result in Nature Medicine, with a UWA press release on Nov 10. Little consumer coverage so far, and it links straight to our proven Strength (590 min) and Bones (244 min) videos.

evidence.signal: Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy for obesity: RCT
T-REX: men and postmenopausal women, supervised resistance exercise plus tirzepatide vs tirzepatide alone

candidates.topic: Keeping results after stopping tirzepatide: SURMOUNT-4 regain, why it varies, and stopping-related heart-risk headlines (observational BMJ Medicine veterans study; Euronews resurfacing, Nov 11)
candidates.angle: Build next to Stopping (8.9% CTR). 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): Keeping Results After You Stop'. Give SURMOUNT-4 exactly (335 vs 335 randomized, +14.0% regain from week 36 to 88, placebo still 9.9% below starting weight). Put the heart headline in context: it's observational, in veterans with type 2 diabetes, linked to up to 22% higher risk vs continuing, not 'double'. Make the plan with your prescriber; no stopping advice.
keywords: what happens when you stop zepbound
candidates.why_now: Euronews ran a 'coming off GLP-1s doubles risk' headline on Nov 11 and the Medscape aftercare story ran on Nov 7. The playbook lists this as a priority Lane A topic.

evidence.signal: Stopping GLP-1 drugs linked to loss of cardiovascular benefit (observational, veterans with T2D)
Up to 22% higher MACE risk after 2 years off vs continuing

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and knee osteoarthritis pain: what's confirmed from TRIUMPH-4 (ACR plenary) and the knee-OA trials
candidates.angle: 13:00 lead Short using the 'what's confirmed?' angle (proven 126–280 views). Average change in pain score vs placebo, the population (obesity plus knee OA), company-reported weight figures. One plain line that it isn't approved and online 'research' products aren't the trial drug.
candidates.why_now: Washington Post column (Nov 11), Medscape, MedPage, Everyday Health and Time are all covering it. Retatrutide Phase 3 data Shorts are proven for us.

evidence.signal: Retatrutide improves knee OA pain and physical function
Powerful new weight-loss drug may ease knee pain, Nov 11

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide vs semaglutide for women over 50: what the head-to-head (SURMOUNT-5, adults with obesity without diabetes) actually showed
candidates.angle: Approved-drug head-to-head search long or Short: tirzepatide-first, obesity population, both arms, open-label. Note that it wasn't designed to test age or sex subgroups unless the paper reports them. Choosing between them is a prescriber conversation.
keywords: which is better mounjaro or wegovy
candidates.why_now: Cincinnati Enquirer piece (Nov 9). Head-to-heads against tirzepatide are a high-demand format in this niche, and tirzepatide-first obesity head-to-head Shorts get 108–176 views for us.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide or tirzepatide? Considerations for women over 50 (Nov 9)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide: what to expect in the first month (nausea timeline, fullness, energy, and when side effects tend to ease)
candidates.angle: Search long using the 'what to expect' timeline format: label language on GI effects being more common during dose increases, what helps, and when to call. No dosing or titration amounts. A gift-season or New Year starter hook works without dating the content.
candidates.why_now: 'What to expect' timelines are among the 10–195x formats in this niche. Publishing in November gives it time to rank before the New Year starter wave.

evidence.signal: GI adverse reactions mostly during dose escalation, with rates vs placebo

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: will it grow back? (label 5.4% vs 0.9%; 7.1% of women vs 0.5% of men)
candidates.angle: Repackage and link the existing Hair long-form, not a new long. One new Short angle allowed after QA verifies the Hair long-form: why hair shedding tends to show up months after rapid weight loss (telogen effluvium timing), per dermatology sources.
candidates.why_now: Our best Short ever (1,023 views). The Rogaine sales-surge story keeps the demand up.

evidence.signal: Alopecia rates by sex vs placebo

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and the thyroid boxed warning: what's confirmed? (Endocrine Reviews review of preclinical and human data, Nov 6)
candidates.angle: Label explainer Short tied to this week's label-change attention. The boxed warning comes from rodent findings; human data so far are reviewed in Endocrine Reviews. Who shouldn't use it (personal or family history of MTC or MEN 2), and which symptoms to report.
candidates.why_now: The eye-warning news is pushing people to read the whole label. A new authoritative review is out, and it has appeared in 4 snapshots.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 RAs and thyroid cancer: review of preclinical and human data

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and lithium: case reports of rising lithium levels (MedShadow, Nov 10; fourth reported tirzepatide case)
candidates.angle: Only a careful 'tell your prescriber about all your medicines' Short, if at all. It's case reports, and eating and drinking less is the leading explanation. Never suggest changing either drug. Lower priority: a niche audience and a case-report evidence level.
candidates.why_now: New case report coverage. Small audience, but a real safety question.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 drugs may interact with lithium; case reports

candidates.topic: REJECT: compounded tirzepatide price report (Ozari), gray-market retatrutide (AJMC, MHRA), 'research use' tirzepatide vials (FDA Philippines advisory), GLP-1 microdosing (ACSH), and generic semaglutide in Brazil and South Africa
candidates.angle: Do not cover. Compounded, gray-market and microdosing topics break brand guardrails, and cost or access stories are banned in long-form.
candidates.why_now: Listed only so downstream agents don't pick them up.

evidence.signal: Ozari compounded tirzepatide price report
